buy-gpu-in-toronto.name: Toronto
buy-gpu-in-toronto.intro: Find the best used GPU deals in Toronto — RTX 3090s, 4090s, 5090s, workstation cards and data-center GPUs listed by sellers across the GTA.

sections.heading: Used GPUs for Toronto's AI scene
sections.body: Toronto is one of North America's busiest AI research hubs, home to the Vector Institute and a deep bench of startups training and serving models. That makes it a strong market for 24GB-and-up cards — buyers here are often after VRAM first, so filter by memory and compare price per GB.

sections.heading: Buy locally, skip the cross-border hassle
sections.body: Buying from a seller in Toronto means no customs brokerage fees on a US shipment and no waiting on a courier. For high-value cards, meeting locally lets you see the card running before money changes hands.

faqs.q: Can I test a used GPU before buying in Toronto?
faqs.a: Many local sellers are happy to demo a card under load. Ask to see it run a benchmark or a few minutes of a stress test, and check temperatures and fan noise.

faqs.q: What if no one in Toronto has the GPU I need?
faqs.a: Post a hardware request with the model, quantity, budget and delivery location. GPUDealer searches its wider supply network across Canada and the US.

buy-gpu-in-calgary.name: Calgary
buy-gpu-in-calgary.intro: Find the best used GPU deals in Calgary — gaming flagships, workstation cards and AI-ready GPUs from sellers across the city.

sections.heading: A growing market for compute hardware
sections.body: Calgary's tech sector has grown quickly, and with it the number of people building local AI rigs and small render or inference boxes. Used high-VRAM cards are the most cost-effective way in, and local listings let you compare condition and price side by side.

sections.heading: Buy from a Calgary seller
sections.body: A local deal means no long-haul shipping risk on a heavy, fragile card. Meeting in person also lets you confirm the exact model, check the PCB and power connectors, and see the card running.

faqs.q: Are used GPUs in Calgary a good deal?
faqs.a: Often, yes — especially previous-generation 24GB cards, which still handle many AI workloads well. Compare listings by VRAM and price per unit before you buy.

faqs.q: Can GPUDealer source GPUs to Calgary in bulk?
faqs.a: Submit a hardware request with the quantity and budget. Multi-GPU requests are exactly what our supply network is built to match.

buy-gpu-in-montreal.name: Montréal
buy-gpu-in-montreal.intro: Find the best used GPU deals in Montréal — RTX cards, workstation GPUs and AI hardware from sellers across the island and the greater Montréal area.

sections.heading: GPUs for one of the world's deep-learning capitals
sections.body: Montréal is home to Mila, one of the largest academic deep-learning research institutes in the world, and a dense cluster of AI labs around it. Researchers and students here need serious VRAM on a budget — which is exactly where the used market shines.

sections.heading: Local deals, fewer surprises
sections.body: Buying from a Montréal seller avoids cross-border shipping and import fees, and lets you inspect a card before paying. For multi-GPU builds, local supply also makes it easier to match identical models.

faqs.q: What GPU is best for AI research on a budget?
faqs.a: Used 24GB cards such as the RTX 3090 remain popular for their VRAM per dollar. If you need more memory, look at 48GB workstation cards like the RTX A6000.

faqs.q: Can I request a specific GPU in Montréal?
faqs.a: Yes — post a hardware request with the model, quantity and budget, and we'll look for matching supply.

buy-gpu-in-london.name: London
buy-gpu-in-london.intro: Find all the great used GPU deals in London — RTX 4090s, 5090s, workstation cards and data-center GPUs from sellers across Greater London.

sections.heading: Hardware for Europe's largest AI hub
sections.body: London hosts Google DeepMind and one of Europe's largest concentrations of AI startups and research teams. Demand for high-VRAM GPUs is strong, and the used market is often the fastest way to get cards in hand without long lead times.

sections.heading: Why buy from a London seller
sections.body: Buying within the UK avoids import VAT and customs charges on hardware shipped from abroad. A local seller also means you can collect in person and confirm the card works before you pay.

faqs.q: Do I pay import fees on a used GPU bought in London?
faqs.a: Not when buying from a seller already in the UK. Import VAT and duty apply to hardware shipped in from outside the UK.

faqs.q: Can GPUDealer source multiple GPUs for a London team?
faqs.a: Submit a hardware request with the model, quantity, budget and timeline. Bulk requests are a priority for our supply network.

buy-gpu-in-chicago.name: Chicago
buy-gpu-in-chicago.intro: Find the best used GPU deals in Chicago — consumer flagships, workstation cards and AI hardware from sellers across Chicagoland.

sections.heading: A major data-center market
sections.body: Chicago is one of the largest data-center markets in the United States, which means a steady flow of enterprise hardware cycling out of service alongside consumer and workstation cards. It's a good place to look for both single GPUs and multi-GPU servers.

sections.heading: Pick up locally
sections.body: A local purchase avoids shipping damage on heavy cards and servers. Meeting a Chicago seller in person lets you verify the model and see the hardware running before you pay.

faqs.q: Where can I buy a used GPU server in Chicago?
faqs.a: Browse current listings on this page, or post a hardware request with the GPU count, model and budget if nothing matches yet.

faqs.q: How do I check a used GPU before buying?
faqs.a: Ask the seller to run a stress test, watch temperatures and clocks, and confirm the model and VRAM in a tool like GPU-Z or nvidia-smi.

buy-gpu-in-new-york.name: New York
buy-gpu-in-new-york.intro: Find the best used GPU deals in New York — RTX cards, workstation GPUs and AI hardware from sellers across the five boroughs.

sections.heading: GPUs for New York's AI and finance teams
sections.body: New York's mix of AI startups, quant and finance firms and media studios creates steady demand for high-end GPUs. Used cards are a fast way to add compute without waiting on new-hardware allocation.

sections.heading: Buy in the city
sections.body: A local seller means no shipping delays or damage risk, and the chance to see the card running before you pay. For larger purchases, it's easier to verify every unit in person.

faqs.q: Is it safe to buy a used GPU in New York?
faqs.a: Meet in a public place, test the card under load before paying, and confirm the model and VRAM match the listing. Every listing on GPUDealer shows where it came from.

faqs.q: Can't find the GPU you want in New York?
faqs.a: Post a hardware request with the model, quantity and budget, and GPUDealer will look across its supply network.

computeHome.metaTitle: Compare GPU Cloud & AI Inference Providers
computeHome.metaDescription: Compare GPU cloud providers, inference APIs and dedicated AI infrastructure — hourly GPU prices, per-token model prices, regions and capabilities.
computeHome.gpuCloudBody: Rent GPUs by the hour. Compare GPU models, hourly rates, regions and on-demand, spot or reserved billing.
computeHome.inferenceBody: Run hosted models through an API. Compare input and output token prices, context length and API features.
computeHome.dedicatedBody: Managed or reserved capacity for your own deployment — usually quote-based, with no public rate card.
computeHome.description: Compare GPU cloud providers, inference APIs and dedicated AI infrastructure. GPUDealer doesn't rent compute — we show you prices with their sources, then link you to the provider.
computeHome.whichGpuCloud: gives you the hardware: a machine with one or more GPUs, billed by the hour. You install and run your own software — the right choice for training, fine-tuning, or serving models you need full control over.
computeHome.whichInference: give you a model: you send requests and pay per token, with no servers to manage. Usually the cheapest way to run popular open models at low or uneven volume.
computeHome.whichDedicated: sits in between — a provider runs the model on capacity reserved for you, for predictable latency and throughput. Pricing is usually by quote.
computeHome.enterpriseBody: Tell us the workload, GPUs or models, volume and budget. We'll come back with options.

returnPolicy.description: GPUDealer doesn't sell or ship hardware. Returns are handled under the policy of the platform or seller where the item is listed.
returnPolicy.s1Heading: GPUDealer doesn't sell or ship hardware
returnPolicy.s1Body: GPUDealer is a discovery platform for used GPUs, AI servers, memory and other compute hardware. We don't own the inventory shown on the site, we don't process payments, and we don't ship items. Because no purchase is made through GPUDealer, we can't accept returns, issue refunds or exchange items.
returnPolicy.s2Body1: Many listings are aggregated from third-party marketplaces such as eBay, Facebook Marketplace and Reddit. Each of these listings shows its source and links to the original listing.
returnPolicy.s2Body2: If you buy one of these items, the purchase happens on that platform, so returns, refunds, disputes and buyer protection follow that platform's policies and the seller's terms there. Check the original listing's return terms before you buy, and contact the seller or the platform directly for any return.
returnPolicy.s3Body: Some listings are posted directly by sellers on GPUDealer. Any sale that results from these listings is arranged between you and the seller, and GPUDealer isn't a party to it. Return terms are whatever you and the seller agree to, so confirm them in writing before you pay.
s4Items: Read the return and refund terms on the original listing.
Confirm the condition, testing history and exact model with the seller.
Prefer payment methods and platforms that offer buyer protection.
Keep records of the listing, your messages and your payment.
returnPolicy.s5Body: If GPUDealer starts processing transactions or shipping hardware, we'll update this policy before those features launch.
